questions.q: Which two chords make a perfect cadence?
questions.why: A perfect cadence is V followed by I.

questions.q: A phrase ends V then vi. Which cadence is this?
questions.why: V to vi is the interrupted cadence: the ear expects I but hears vi.

questions.q: A piece in C major introduces F♯ and cadences in G major. What has happened?
questions.why: G is the dominant of C and has F♯ in its key signature.

questions.model: A note held over from one chord into the next, creating a dissonance with the new chord, which then resolves by falling one step.
points: note held over/tied into the next chord causing a clash
